title.en: Find the speed of a transverse wave on a string
Find the speed of sound; explain Laplace's correction

say.en: A veena player turns the peg to tighten a string and the note goes up. Tension changes how fast waves run along the string. In this lesson: Find the speed of a transverse wave on a string.
Find the speed of sound; explain Laplace's correction.

body.en: The speed of a *transverse wave* on a stretched string depends only on the tension T and the mass per unit length μ: v = √(T/μ). Tension provides the restoring force and μ the inertia. It does not depend on the frequency; the source decides the frequency, and the wavelength then adjusts as λ = v/ν.
body.kn: ಎಳೆದ ತಂತಿಯ ಮೇಲಿನ ಅಡ್ಡ ತರಂಗದ ಜವ v = √(T/μ). ಎಳೆತ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಬಲ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ, μ ಜಡತ್ವ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಜವ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title.en: What sets the speed of a wave

say.en: A string with mass per unit length mu is stretched over a pulley by a hanging load. The tension T pulls it back; mu resists.
Only T and mu matter, and dimensions fix the answer: T over mu has units of a speed squared.
A steel wire 0.72 metre long of mass 5 grams under a tension of 60 newton: the speed is about 93 metres per second.
Sound in a fluid travels at root of B over rho. Newton took B = P, as if the compressions were isothermal, and got only about 280 metres per second.
Laplace: the compressions are too fast for heat to flow, so they are adiabatic and B = gamma P. That gives about 332 metres per second, matching experiment.

body.en: Longitudinal waves travel at v = √(B/ρ) in a fluid and √(Y/ρ) in a solid rod. Newton assumed the compressions in air were isothermal (B = P) and got about 280 m s⁻¹, too low. Laplace pointed out they are so fast that they are adiabatic (B = γP), giving v = √(γP/ρ) ≈ 331 m s⁻¹ at 0 °C, which matches experiment. For a gas, v does not depend on pressure at a fixed temperature, and v ∝ √T.

heading.en: Speed of Waves and the Principle of Superposition

tagline.en: Speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string, speed of sound in solids, liquids and gases, Newton's formula and Laplace's correction, and the principle of superposition with interference.

myth.en: Sound travels faster when air pressure is higher, because the molecules are packed more closely.

truth.en: At a fixed temperature, the speed of sound in a gas does not depend on pressure. It depends on temperature: $v = \sqrt{\gamma RT/M}$. Higher pressure does make the gas stiffer (larger $B = \gamma P$), but it also makes it denser in exactly the same ratio, so $\gamma P/\rho$ is unchanged. Sound is slower on a high mountain because the air there is colder, not because the pressure is lower.

say.en: String: $v = \sqrt{T/\mu}$, set by the medium, not by the source.
Fluids: $v = \sqrt{B/\rho}$; rods: $v = \sqrt{Y/\rho}$. Sound is fastest in solids.
Laplace: sound in a gas is adiabatic, $v = \sqrt{\gamma P/\rho}$; independent of pressure, $\propto \sqrt{T}$, slightly higher in humid air.
Superposition: displacements add. Two equal waves with phase difference $\phi$ give amplitude $2a\cos(\phi/2)$.

goal.en: Speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string, speed of sound in solids, liquids and gases, Newton's formula and Laplace's correction, and the principle of superposition with interference.

points.kn: ಧ್ವನಿ: v = √(γP/ρ), 0 °C ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಮಾರು 331 m s⁻¹.

points.en: Speed of sound ∝ √T, independent of P at fixed T.
points.kn: ಧ್ವನಿಯ ಜವ ∝ √T; ಸ್ಥಿರ T ನಲ್ಲಿ P ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

homework.en: A string of mass 2.5 g and length 1 m is under a tension of 100 N. Find the speed of waves on it.

narration.en: Recap. String: v = √(T/μ). Sound: v = √(γP/ρ) (Laplace), about 331 m s⁻¹ at 0 °C. Speed of sound ∝ √T, independent of P at fixed T.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ತಂತಿ: v = √(T/μ). ಧ್ವನಿ: v = √(γP/ρ), 0 °C ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಮಾರು 331 m s⁻¹. ಧ್ವನಿಯ ಜವ ∝ √T; ಸ್ಥಿರ T ನಲ್ಲಿ P ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

title.kn: ಅಧ್ಯಾರೋಪಣ ತತ್ವ, ತರಂಗಗಳ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲನ ಮತ್ತು ನಿಂತ ತರಂಗಗಳು

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. String: v equals the square root of (T/ micro).
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ತಂತಿ: v equals the square root of (T/ micro).

say.en: Sound: v equals the square root of (gamma P/ rho) Laplace, about 331 metres s to the power minus 1 at 0 degrees Celsius.
say.kn: ಧ್ವನಿ: v equals the square root of (gamma P/ rho), 0 degrees Celsius ನಲ್ಲಿ ಸುಮಾರು 331 metres s to the power minus 1.

say.en: Speed of sound is proportional to the square root of T, independent of P at fixed T.
say.kn: ಧ್ವನಿಯ ಜವ is proportional to the square root of T; ಸ್ಥಿರ T ನಲ್ಲಿ P ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
